fire:
The river runs beneath the hill,
The mill wheel turning slow and still,
And all the valley sleeps tonight,
Beneath the moon's unhurried light.

We marched along the dusty road,
Each soldier bent beneath his load,
And sang of home and those we knew,
As evening fell in shades of blue.

Oh little bird upon the bough,
What song is in your heart just now?
You sing of spring and skies so wide,
And fields where golden poppies hide.

The apples hang so round and red,
The children dance in the orchard bed,
And mother calls them in to tea,
Beneath the spreading cherry tree.

With lanterns lit we sailed away,
Across the cold and silver bay,
And never once looked back to shore,
Where we had lived for years before.

Our daily bread is plain and brown,
We eat it in the sleepy town,
A little cheese, a cup of wine,
And all the evening feels so fine.

The snow falls soft on roof and lane,
It hides the fields and fills the drain,
And every child that wakes to see,
Runs out to play beneath the tree.

I wandered where the willows grow,
Beside the stream so cool and slow,
And there I found a quiet place,
Where time itself could slow its pace.
quiet: The river runs beneath the hill, and the mill wheel turns slowly while the whole valley sleeps under the moon.
We marched along the dusty road for hours, each soldier carrying a heavy load and talking about home.
A small bird sat on the branch outside the window and sang for most of the morning.
The apples in the orchard were round and red, and the children played there until their mother called them in.
We lit the lanterns and sailed across the bay, and nobody looked back at the town we had left.
Our breakfast is usually plain brown bread with a little cheese and a cup of tea.
The snow fell softly on the roofs and lanes, and the children ran outside as soon as they woke up.
I walked along the stream where the willows grow and found a quiet place to sit for a while.
